plot: The morning after her birthday Pip gets her driving lesson up Wheelburg Hill, but she keeps stopping at the big bump halfway; Turbo's 'just zoom' idea is off the table now that he's a crossing guard, Grumpy says everyone gets stuck there, and Bolt's slow-and-steady lessons don't fix it; the twist is that Pip isn't scared of the hill at all but of the 'big drop' Bertha cheerfully warned about, which she can't see past the top; Bolt tells her to ask instead of guess, drives beside her over the top, and the 'drop' is a gentle little road to the duck pond; lesson: when you can't see what's next, ask, don't guess; then from the top Pip spots a moving truck next to her house — who is moving in?

script.title: Can Pip Drive Up the Big Hill Alone?

set.place: Wheelburg Hill road from the bakery up to the top, early morning

script.description: Pip's first driving lesson up Wheelburg Hill, and why she keeps stopping at the bump. Inspector Bolt #17

beats.say: I'm rolling backwards! Bolt! Bolt! Help me!
Gentle brakes, Pip! Gentle! There. You stopped. You're safe.

beats.text: CAN PIP CLIMB THE BIG HILL?

beats.say: It was the morning after Pip's birthday.
Her present was a driving lesson. Up Wheelburg Hill. All by herself.
I got to the big bump. Then I rolled back.
Can a little car like me really reach the top alone?
Not if you rush. But if you go slow? Yes.
Lesson one. Low gear. Slow and steady.
No, no! Lesson one is speed! Zoom up before the hill notices!
Turbo. You are a crossing guard now.
Right. Sorry. Slow and steady. Boring. But safe!
Good luck, Pip! My shift starts now. Honk from the top!
And Turbo drove off, very slowly, to the school corner.
Then Big Bertha rolled up, full of morning school bags.
Pip, dear! Driving up the big hill today? Ooh, be careful!
On the other side, there's a big drop! Whoooosh!
A big... drop?
Bye-bye! The school bell won't wait for me!
Pip didn't say a word. But her little wheels went very still.
Ready for try number two?
Ready. Low gear. Slow and steady.
Pip started up the hill. Bolt drove right behind her.
Past the bakery. Past the red mailbox. Up, up, up.
Wonderful, Pip! Eyes up! Look at the road ahead!
I'm doing it! I'm really, really doing it!
Then came the big bump. With the orange cone on top.
And Pip stopped. Right next to the cone. Again.
I can't! If I keep going, I'll go over the top!
Going over the top is the whole idea, Pip.
I mean... my engine is tired. That's all.
Your engine sounds perfect. I am a detective. I listen.
If we don't find the reason, you'll stop here every time.
So they rolled back down, slowly, to the bottom of the hill.
Grumpy was parked there, having his morning nap.
Hmph. Stuck at the bump? Everybody gets stuck at the bump.
Even you, Grumpy?
Not me. I tow the ones who get stuck. Different job.
Pip, every stop has a reason. Let's find yours.
There's no reason. I'm just small. Small cars can't do big hills.
Your wheels are small. Your engine is strong. I checked.
Small engine, big noise. Like Turbo. Go on, kid.
Then why does my engine want to stop at the bump?
Try once more. This time, tell me everything you see.
Try number three. Low gear. Slow and steady.
I see the bakery. I see the mailbox. I see the cone.
And at the big bump, Pip stopped. Again.
What do you see now, Pip? Up there, at the top?
Nothing! Just sky! I can't see what's there! That's the scary part!
Over the top there's a big drop. Bertha said so!
Bolt was quiet for a moment. Then he smiled under his hat.
Pip. Have you ever seen this big drop?
No. I only imagined it. It got bigger every time.
When you can't see what's next, don't guess. Ask.
So. Ask me.
Bolt... what is on the other side of the hill?
Come and see. This time I'll drive right next to you.
Side by side, they crept over the big bump.
Up. Up. Up. Until the sky was all around them.
On the other side? A gentle little road. Down to the duck pond.
That's it? That little slope is the big drop?
Bertha calls every slope a big drop. And every puddle a lake.
I was scared of a duck pond road! A tiny one!
Then Bertha came puffing up the hill, honking happily.
Pip! You made it! Did you see my big drop? Whoosh!
I saw it, Bertha. It's a very small big drop.
Oh dear. Did my whoosh scare you, Pip? I'm so sorry!
A little. But I asked Bolt. And now I know.
Far below, from the school corner, came a tiny honk.
Beep beep, Turbo! I'm at the top! All by myself!
Almost by yourself. Next time, I'll stay at the bottom.
Remember: when you can't see what's next, ask. Don't guess.
Ask, don't guess. And low gear. Slow and steady!
And this is for the bravest little driver in Wheelburg.
A gold star! My very first hill star!
Pip looked down at all of Wheelburg. Everything looked so small.
And then she saw something new. Next to her little house.
A big moving truck. And a big pile of boxes.
Bolt! Somebody is moving in next door! Who is it?
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!
